## Claude Code Hooks System

Claude Code provides a comprehensive hook system with **26 event types** [14]:

| Category | Events |
|----------|--------|
| Session lifecycle | SessionStart, SessionEnd |
| User interaction | UserPromptSubmit, Elicitation, ElicitationResult |
| Tool execution | PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied |
| Agent control | SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, StopFailure |
| Task management | TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle |
| Configuration | InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged |
| File system | FileChanged, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove |
| Context management | PreCompact, PostCompact |
| Notifications | Notification |

### Exit Code Semantics

| Exit Code | Behavior | Use Case |
|-----------|----------|----------|
| 0 | Action proceeds; stdout added to context (for UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart) | Informational hooks |
| 2 | Action **BLOCKED**; stderr becomes feedback to Claude | Quality gates |
| Other | Action proceeds; transcript shows error notice | Soft warnings |

### Hook Types

| Type | Description | Determinism |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| command | Shell command execution | Deterministic |
| http | HTTP endpoint call | Deterministic |
| prompt | Single-turn LLM evaluation | Non-deterministic |
| agent | Multi-turn LLM with tools | Non-deterministic |

### Key Behaviors

- Multiple matching hooks run **in parallel**; identical commands deduplicated [14]
- Most restrictive answer wins (deny > ask > allow) [14]
- PreToolUse fires **before** permission-mode check — enforces even in bypassPermissions mode [14]
- "allow" does NOT override deny rules from settings — hooks can tighten but not loosen [14]
- PostToolUse cannot undo actions [14]
- When multiple PreToolUse hooks return updatedInput, last to finish wins (non-deterministic) [14]
- Matcher supports tool name filtering (PreToolUse/PostToolUse), session start type, and `if` field for argument-level filtering (v2.1.85+) [14]

## CLAUDE.md vs Hooks Distinction

A critical architectural distinction:

| Mechanism | Nature | Enforcement | Bypass Risk |
|-----------|--------|-------------|-------------|
| CLAUDE.md | Prompt instructions | Agent follows voluntarily | Agent can ignore or misinterpret |
| Hooks | Mechanical gates | System-enforced (exit 2 = block) | Cannot be bypassed by agent |

CLAUDE.md provides guides (feedforward) [15] — instructions that shape agent behavior. Hooks provide sensors and gates (feedback) [15] — mechanical enforcement that operates regardless of agent compliance.

superpowers [19] operates at the CLAUDE.md/prompt level. tdd-guard [20] operates at the hooks level. Both enforce TDD, but with fundamentally different reliability guarantees.

## Harness Engineering (Fowler)

Fowler's framework [15] defines "Agent = Model + Harness" — everything except the model itself.

### Guides vs Sensors

| Control Type | Direction | Example | Source |
|--------------|-----------|---------|--------|
| Guides (feedforward) | Anticipate and prevent | CLAUDE.md instructions, approved fixtures | [15] |
| Sensors (feedback) | Observe and correct | Test results, linter output, review agents | [15] |

> "Separately, you get either an agent that keeps repeating the same mistakes (feedback-only) or an agent that encodes rules but never finds out whether they worked." [15]

### Execution Types

| Type | Speed | Determinism | Examples | Source |
|------|-------|-------------|----------|--------|
| Computational | ms-seconds | Deterministic | Tests, linters, type checkers | [15] |
| Inferential | Slower | Non-deterministic | Code review agents, LLM-as-judge | [15] |

### Regulation Categories

| Category | Focus | Maturity | Source |
|----------|-------|----------|--------|
| Maintainability Harness | Internal code quality | Mature | [15] |
| Architecture Fitness Harness | Fitness functions | Moderate | [15] |
| Behaviour Harness | Functional correctness | Least mature | [15] |

**CORRECTION:** The Anthropic harness blog [12] describes a **TWO-part** system (initializer agent + coding agent), not three as sometimes claimed.

## Gate Ordering: "Keep Quality Left"

Fowler's framework [15] defines gate ordering by cost and speed:

| Stage | Checks | Speed | Examples |
|-------|--------|-------|----------|
| Pre-commit / Pre-integration | Fast, cheap | ms-seconds | Linters, basic review agents, fast test suites |
| Post-integration pipeline | Expensive sensors | Minutes | Mutation testing, broad code review |
| Continuous monitoring | Drift detection | Ongoing | Dead code scanning, dependency scanning, SLO degradation |

This maps directly to Claude Code hooks:
- **PreToolUse hooks** = pre-commit gates (fast, blocking)
- **PostToolUse hooks** = post-integration sensors (observational)
- **Stop hooks** = end-of-task validation

## Pre-commit + CI Composition

The integration pattern layers multiple enforcement mechanisms:

```
Layer 1: CLAUDE.md instructions (guides — prompt-level)
Layer 2: PreToolUse hooks (gates — tool-level, blocking)
Layer 3: PostToolUse hooks (sensors — tool-level, observational)
Layer 4: pre-commit hooks (gates — git-level, blocking)
Layer 5: CI pipeline (sensors — integration-level)
Layer 6: Continuous monitoring (sensors — production-level)
```

tdd-guard [20] operates at Layer 2 — intercepting Write/Edit/MultiEdit before they execute. pre-commit frameworks (pydevtools [42], standard pre-commit) operate at Layer 4 — catching issues at commit time.

The distinction matters: Layer 2 catches problems during generation (cheaper to fix), while Layer 4 catches them at commit (after the agent has potentially built on bad code).

## Parallel Subagent Review

Claude Code supports subagent hooks (SubagentStart, SubagentStop events) [14], enabling:
- Multiple review agents running in parallel on different quality dimensions
- Each subagent applying specialized review criteria
- Results aggregated with most-restrictive-wins semantics [14]

The orchestrator-workers pattern [11] maps naturally: a central agent dispatches code to specialized review subagents (security, style, correctness), each returning findings.

## Practical Integration Examples

### TDD Enforcement via Hooks
tdd-guard [20] hooks into PreToolUse to intercept file modifications. On exit code 2, the write is blocked and stderr provides feedback to Claude explaining why [14][20].

### Spec-First via CLAUDE.md
spec-kit [18] integrates through CLAUDE.md instructions and task generation — operating at the guide level [15]. TDD ordering is optional: "If tests are requested, test tasks are included and ordered to be written before implementation" [18].

### Multi-Layer Quality Gate
Combining superpowers [19] (prompt-level TDD enforcement) + tdd-guard [20] (hook-level enforcement) + Ruff [21] (pre-commit linting) + CI tests creates defense in depth — if the agent ignores the prompt instruction, the hook catches it; if the hook is misconfigured, pre-commit catches it.

## Anthropic Long-Running Agent Harness

The Anthropic harness for long-running agents [12] implements:
1. **Initializer Agent:** runs once — sets up infrastructure (init.sh, progress files, initial git commit, feature requirements) [12]
2. **Coding Agent:** operates in subsequent sessions for incremental progress [12]

> "Each new session begins with no memory of what came before" — compensated by persistent documentation (git logs, progress files) [12]

Quality patterns include state verification (sessions begin by running E2E tests), feature tracking (JSON pass/fail), and strong guardrails preventing inappropriate modifications [12].

## Gaps and Limitations

- pydevtools hooks guide [42] was not fetched for detailed verification
- SonarQube AI Code Assurance [37] details not fetched
- No published study measures the quality impact of layered enforcement (hooks + pre-commit + CI) vs single-layer
- Hook ordering within a layer (multiple PreToolUse hooks) is parallel with non-deterministic updatedInput resolution [14] — this can cause race conditions in complex configurations
- PostToolUse hooks cannot undo actions [14] — they are sensors only, not gates
- The prompt-level vs hook-level enforcement reliability difference is not empirically quantified
- Anthropic harness blog describes a TWO-part system [12], not the three-part system cited in some secondary sources
- Inferential hooks (prompt/agent types) introduce non-determinism and latency into the quality gate pipeline [14][15]
- No benchmark exists for optimal gate ordering in agentic Python workflows
